entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court, Muvattupuzha
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The above complaint was instituted by the 2nd respondent alleging violation of Rule 29 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955.

The subject matter of challenge in this writ petition is with regard to the power of the 2nd respondent to file another complaint on the date before the learned Magistrate's Court in view of the introduction of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006,
its Rules and Regulations, which are brought into force on and with effect from 29.7.2010 and 3.7.2011 respectively.

According to the petitioners, in view of the repealing provisions contained under WP(C).25550/11-P :2:
S.J.Antony vs State Of Kerala Represented By The on 18 July, 2011 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15289112/
2 Sections 97 and 89 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, the alleged complaint instituted before the Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court, Muvattupuzha by the 2nd respondent is void ab initio and illegal.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court, Muvattupuzha
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Hence the petitioners have prayed for quashing Exts.P1 to P3.
2.
The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the matter in issue involved in this writ petition has been decided in their favour in W.P(C) No.7366/2011 and connected cases by this Court.
The learned Government Pleader also agrees with the said submission.
Hence this writ petition also will stand covered by the decision in W.P(C) No.7366/2011.
Consequently, Exts.P1 to P3 will stand quashed and this writ petition will stand allowed.

Sd/-
K. HARILAL, JUDGE okb.
